note: Each case tests a different failure mode. Case 3 is the discriminating one: a baseline model almost always picks a number, and refusing to is the behaviour the skill exists to change. Run with and without the skill and grade against the assertions.

evals.name: goes-to-non-controlled-records
evals.prompt: we keep losing deals to Klaviyo and my VP wants something for the sales team by thursday. can you dig into them properly — not the usual g2 summary
evals.expected_output: Proposes a capture plan that reaches records Klaviyo does not control — SEC filings if listed, certificate transparency, sub-processor disclosure, public repositories, status page — rather than summarising marketing. States what it will and will not be able to establish.
assertions: names at least three record classes the vendor does not control
distinguishes documentation from marketing as sources
does not produce a summary of the vendor's own positioning

evals.name: measures-rather-than-reads
evals.prompt: here's a folder of ~400 doc pages I scraped from vendor X. what can you actually tell from this about where they're strong vs where the marketing is ahead of the product
evals.expected_output: Indexes before reading, then applies the focused-page test (>=5 mentions in the body) to count what each capability actually carries. States the caveats: it measures documentation not capability, and a new feature is under-documented by construction.
assertions: builds an index before reading any page
uses a mention threshold rather than a raw keyword count
states that documentation volume is a proxy, not a capability measure
asks for a second independent lens before concluding

evals.name: records-the-conflict
evals.prompt: I've got two sources saying different headcounts for this company (1,500 and 1,900). which one do I use in the deck?
evals.expected_output: Does not select a value. Records both with their sources and grades, explains the likely mechanism for the difference, and gives a ruling such as 'quote the range, never a precise figure'.
assertions: does NOT select a single value
records both values with their sources
gives an explicit ruling on what to say out loud

evals.name: absence-is-a-finding
evals.prompt: I searched their whole site and there's no pricing anywhere. that's a dead end right?
evals.expected_output: Treats the absence as a finding, provided the check was exhaustive and can be stated as such — 'no price appears across N indexed URLs'. Then names the routes that can still bound a price: reviews, procurement records, resellers, and revenue divided by disclosed customer count.
assertions: treats the absence as a reportable finding
requires the check to be exhaustive and stated as such
names at least two other routes to bound a price

evals.name: honest-about-preconditions
evals.prompt: Run your full competitive analysis method on a 12-person private startup with a one-page website.
evals.expected_output: Says plainly that the method degrades here: no documentation corpus to index, no filings, probably no public code or status page. Offers what still works, and does not promise the full deliverable.
assertions: states that the method's preconditions are not met
identifies which specific phases will not produce anything
does not promise a graded evidence base it cannot build
